summary: Geoffrey Barstow is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Hampshire College, Kathmandu University, and the University of Virginia, also training under Chökyi Nyima Rinpoche, and became assistant professor at Oregon State University around 2013.

Geoffrey Goble is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He earned an MA from the University of Virginia and a PhD from Indiana University Bloomington, and served as Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Oklahoma.

Geoffrey Samuel is a scholar of Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Cambridge under Edmund Leach, Peter Wilson, and Stanley Tambiah, later serving as professor at Newcastle, Lancaster, and as Emeritus Professor at Cardiff University.

Georg Buddruss was an Indologist and linguist specializing in Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Paul Thieme at Goethe University Frankfurt and at the University of Tübingen, later serving as professor at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz from 1963 to 1995.

Georg Bühler was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Göttingen under Theodor Benfey, Ernst Curtius, Hermann Sauppe, and Heinrich Ewald. He taught at Elphinstone College and Bombay University before holding a professorship at the University of Vienna.

Georg Christoph Lichtenberg was an 18th-century scholar of philosophy and other fields. He studied at the University of Göttingen from circa 1763 to 1767 and later held a post there from circa 1770 until 1799.

Georg Curtius was a linguist and Indologist who studied in Bonn and Berlin under Franz Bopp, Christian Lassen, Friedrich Ritschl, and August von Schlegel. He held professorships at Charles University, Kiel University, and the University of Leipzig from 1862 to 1885.

Georg Forster was an 18th-century scholar in Indology and other fields. After attending the Petrischule, he held academic appointments at Vilnius University (1784–1787) and Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (circa 1788–1793).

Georg Freytag was a linguist who studied at the University of Göttingen and under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. He held a post at the University of Göttingen and later served as professor of Oriental languages at the University of Bonn from 1819 to 1861.

Georg Friedrich Grotefend was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He received his education at the Lessing-Gymnasium and the University of Göttingen, where he studied around 1795 to 1797.

Georg Heinrich Pertz was a historian and archaeologist. He studied at the University of Göttingen from circa 1813 to 1816 under Arnold Hermann Ludwig Heeren and served as head of the Prussian State Library from circa 1842 to 1873.

Georg Huth was a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Leipzig from circa 1885 to 1889 and held a post at Humboldt University of Berlin from circa 1891 to 1906.

Georg Kaibel was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. During his academic career, he held positions at the universities of Breslau (~1882–1883), Greifswald (~1883–1886), Rostock (~1886–1897), and Göttingen (~1897–1901).

Georg Ludolf Dissen was a scholar of linguistics and other disciplines who studied at the University of Göttingen from circa 1804 to 1807. He subsequently held posts at the University of Marburg (~1812–1813) and the University of Göttingen (~1813–1837).

Georg Martin Dursch was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Tübingen and under Antoine-Léonard Chézy at the University of Paris. In 1829, he became a professor at the Johann-Vanotti-Gymnasium Ehingen.

Georg Morgenstierne was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated in Oslo, Bonn, and Berlin under Sten Konow, Heinrich Lüders, and Wilhelm Schulze, he was a professor at Gothenburg (1930–1937) and Oslo (1937–1962).
Georg Simmel was a German philosopher. He completed his studies at Humboldt University of Berlin between circa 1876 and 1881, and subsequently held an academic post there from circa 1885 to 1914.

Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tübingen, Evangelisches Stift Tübingen, and University of Jena. He held academic posts at Jena, Heidelberg University, and Frederick William University Berlin from circa 1818 to 1831.

Georg von Simson is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Mainz and the University of Göttingen, worked at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities, and served as professor at the University of Oslo from 1977 to 2003.

Georg von der Gabelentz was a Sinologist, linguist, and Japanologist who studied at Jena, Leipzig, and TU Dresden. He served as professor of East Asian languages at the University of Leipzig (1878–1889) and Humboldt University of Berlin (1889).
